title: session mosaic: sdk handshake and mini-frames brainstorm
content:
Context:
This is a working brainstorm for a new lightweight session model we're calling "Session Mosaic". Goal: enable high-throughput partial output delivery (mini-frames) plus safe tool-calling and offline replayability while keeping SDK ergonomics simple for web and mobile. This doc collects ideas, tradeoffs, and an initial API sketch to iterate on with eng and DX.

Background / motivation:
- Many customers want the UX benefits of streaming partial outputs (progressive highlights, tool invitations, previewed results) but are frustrated by complex client-side state machines and large bandwidth spikes.
- Existing partial-response protocols we considered either force clients to handle many frame types or make resumability expensive.
- Tool-calling and structured outputs complicate streaming: tool invites may arrive mid-stream, and clients need to reconcile partial state deterministically for offline replay and debuggability.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Compact framing: small, typed mini-frames that are cheap to send/receive and easy to merge into a client transcript.
- Deterministic replay: every session produces a canonical event sequence that can be rehydrated offline to re-run tool calls or reproduce UI.
- Low SDK surface area: a small set of primitives (onFrame, onCheckpoint, resumeSession) that work across web, mobile, and server SDKs.
- Tool-call safety: explicit handshake for tool invocation that avoids duplication and supports idempotent retries.
- Bandwidth budgeting: frames designed to degrade gracefully under bandwidth limits (e.g., summaries instead of full partials).

Key concepts:
- Mini-frame: smallest increment of server-to-client output. Types: text, token, annotation, schema-patch, tool-invite, tool-result, checkpoint. Each frame has a monotonically increasing sequence id (within session) and a compact header (type, seq, annotations).
- Mosaic snapshot: periodic compact checkpoints (every N frames or after semantic boundaries) that contain a compact summary and pointers to the last applied tool states and KV cache tag. Useful for fast resume and offline view.
- Handshake tokens: ephemeral tokens attached to tool-invite frames (tool_invite_id) that uniquely identify the server-side intent. Clients include the token when invoking a tool to ensure idempotency.
- Typed patches: structured-output patches (JSON-LD or typed schema) expressed as a small patch language for merging into client models without re-parsing full responses.

API/SDK ergonomics (sketch):
- JS/TS SDK surface (minimal):
  * startSession(params) -> SessionHandle
  * SessionHandle.onFrame(fn(frame)) // incremental frames, lightweight
  * SessionHandle.onCheckpoint(fn(snapshot)) // durable snapshots
  * SessionHandle.callTool(tool_invite_token, args) -> promise(tool_result)
  * SessionHandle.resumeSession(session_id, options) -> resumed handle

- Mobile (Swift/Kotlin): same primitives but with platform-idiomatic callbacks and a small resilient background resume helper for network churn.

Frame semantics (examples):
- text-frame: {seq: 124, type: "text", delta: "…"} // small text delta
- annotation-frame: {seq: 125, type: "annotation", span: [10, 23], label: "suggested_action"}
- tool-invite: {seq: 130, type: "tool-invite", tool: "search-smd", invite_id: "ti_12", hint: "did you mean…"} // server promises to accept one matching tool call per invite_id
- tool-result: {seq: 131, type: "tool-result", invite_id: "ti_12", status: "ok", payload_ref: "blob://…"}
- checkpoint: {seq: 140, type: "checkpoint", snapshot_ref: "snap://…", last_tool_ids: ["ti_12"]} // lightweight reference to reconstruct state

Operational/implementation notes:
- Backpressure: clients may set a budget (max_bytes_per_sec or max_frames) when starting sessions. Server adapts by emitting summarized frames (summary-frame with stable id) instead of more granular partials.
- Storage: checkpoints are persisted for a bounded TTL (configurable per-customer). Avoid persisting full token-level transcripts by default; store compact snapshots and references to archived blobs.
- Tool idempotency: enforcement rule: server guarantees a single canonical tool_invite id per logical invite. If a client calls with the same invite token multiple times, server returns the canonical result or an explicit duplicate error.
- Security: tool_invite tokens scoped to session and short-lived. Tool invocations require appropriate project credentials; private tool endpoints never receive user prompt text in raw form unless flagged by customer policy.

Developer UX examples / flows:
1) Mobile chat typing preview:
   - startSession -> onFrame receives small token deltas; SDK buffers small tokens and exposes incremental 'typing' preview UI.
   - network flake -> SDK auto-resume with resumeSession(session_id). Server responds with a checkpoint snapshot; client merges and resumes incremental frames.
2) In-chat tool suggestion and safe accept:
   - model emits tool-invite frame with invite_id and a short hint.
   - UI shows accept button; if user taps, SDK.callTool(invite_id, {args}) ensures request includes token; server returns tool-result frame which is appended to stream.
3) Offline replay for debugging:
   - Console UI fetches the stored checkpoint and replay frames from snapshot_ref to rehydrate canonical interaction for audit and eval.

Telemetry and observability:
- Instrumentation: frames emitted, frames dropped (due to budget), resume attempts, tool-invite accepted/declined, tool-call latency and errors. Tag telemetry with model_id, session_type, customer_id.
- Console: new per-session timeline view showing mini-frame boundaries, checkpoint markers, and tool-invite lifecycles. Helpful for debugging client-replay mismatches.

Rollout plan (rough):
- Phase 0 (experiment): prototype in internal beta with a small set of customers that need resumable streaming (Q2 2025). Limited to text+tool-invite frames, no persisted checkpoints by default.
- Phase 1: add typed patches and checkpoint persistence, SDK helpers for resume (Q3 2025). Collect telemetry and early SDK feedback.
- Phase 2: full public launch with Console timeline UI and admin controls for checkpoint TTLs and bandwidth budgets (Q4 2025).

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How big should a checkpoint be vs relying on on-demand re-run? Store more state for faster resume vs store less to reduce storage costs.
- Patch format: adopt existing schema diff (JSON Patch) vs design a compact typed patch language. Tradeoff: interoperability vs compactness.
- Tool-handshake flow: do we allow client-side local validation of tool arguments prior to calling server? Risk: inconsistent validation logic across clients.
- Cross-region resume: can a session resume in another region? If yes, we must replicate snapshots or provide cross-region access policies.

Next steps / action items:
- Product: finalize goals and minimal success criteria for Phase 0 (owner: Aisha).
- Eng (runtime): spike a mini-frame transport over existing streaming infra; validate backpressure heuristics (owner: Ben).
- DX / SDK: prototype the startSession/onFrame compact API in JS and Kotlin; gather ergonomics feedback (owner: Rosa).
- SRE / infra: draft retention and cost model for snapshot storage (owner: Miguel).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an intentionally exploratory doc. I want feedback on the framing (mini-frame vs larger incremental chunks), the tool-invite idempotency model, and whether the checkpoint snapshot approach is feasible within our current kernel and storage constraints.
- If you're in eng and want to prototype, ping me in #hosted-session-mosaic.

Appendix: quick checklist for experiments:
- [ ] Implement minimal mini-frame encoder/decoder in JS SDK (text, tool-invite, checkpoint).
- [ ] Create a prototype server that emits summarized frames when client budget < threshold.
- [ ] Wire telemetry events for resume attempts and dropped frames.
- [ ] Add a Console view for a single session timeline (prototype only).

End of brainstorm.
